Accrual accounting records income and expenses when they happen, not when cash moves. If you sell something on credit, you record the sale when you deliver the product or service, even if you’ll be paid later. If you incur an expense, you record it when you owe it, not when you pay the bill. Cash-basis accounting does the opposite: it records income only when you actually receive cash, and records expenses only when you actually pay.

Accrual gives a clearer picture of how your business is doing over time because it links sales with the costs to make them. That makes it better for growing businesses or when customers pay later. Cash-basis is simpler and shows your actual bank balance, which can be useful for very small operations or sole proprietors. In short: accrual shows what’s earned and owed now; cash shows what’s been paid and received now.
